label: aligned

evidence.quote: adapters/live.py has never reached that endpoint from here

finding: Every mechanism the question names is now read back out of a transcript of real loopback HTTP traffic - an authorization server and two protected-resource servers each on their own TCP port, an ordinary HTTP client on the other end - rather than out of configuration or two halves of a flow calling each other's methods: the 401's protected-resource pointer, protected-resource and authorization-server metadata discovery, PKCE S256 enforced server-side before the code is redeemed, a resource indicator on the authorization request and on both token requests including the refresh, the refreshed token's decoded audience naming only the target server, that same token refused 403 by the second server, a single POST /mcp endpoint accepting the streamable content type with no separate event-stream endpoint, and a tool result checked against its declared output schema. Deliberate breakages make the gate say no (refresh-omit-resource fails exactly the refresh's resource check, 13/14, exit 1; dropping PKCE cascades to 6/14 because the server refuses the redemption), and the whole set is wired into the capability's gate, which passes 43/43 - and the adapter that speaks to a real endpoint is the one exercised, sourcing its bearer token from that same exchange rather than a second implementation of it. That meets the aligned anchor's letter, including the resource indicator on refresh and schema-validated results. It stops short of leading because both ends of the wire are this repo's own code: the exchange is verified against a deployment this file starts, no surface outside this repo has ever been reached, so the transport is asserted from the client's own request shape rather than negotiated with a server this platform does not control, and the static bearer token with no audience binding survives as the default whenever the discovery flag is unset.
